page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7nex.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on KVM virtualization within the vendor's Enhanced family. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor featuring an x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, 16.0 GB of system memory delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and an allocation of 48 MB of L3 cache. The CPU features vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI extensions. It includes no bundled local storage and no hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard computing cores, with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data demonstrates typical single-threaded capability accompanied by constrained multi-threaded scaling due to the 2-core physical limit. Single-core performance sits in the middle tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1548.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1882.09. Cryptographic throughput remains balanced, producing a PassMark encryption rating of 3642.21 and an average PassMark memory score of 2075.54. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks show weak relative throughput, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 3326.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 3860.98. Intensive parallelism is limited, as shown by lower performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 20.24 GB/sec and Clang compilation at 4219.0.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance provides predictable performance with dedicated execution resources and a reliable 5 Gbps baseline network, avoiding the throttling common to burstable tiers. Because it lacks local NVMe disks, all persistent data requires external block storage volumes, which trade raw IOPS for decoupled operational flexibility. The 1:4 core-to-memory configuration delivers balanced resource allocation without paying a premium for excess memory or idle accelerator hardware.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7nex.xlarge is suited for standard general-purpose cloud duties. Typical deployments include web and API serving, intermediate microservice hosting, lightweight enterprise applications, standard CI/CD build tasks, and staging environments where moderate compute and standard memory footprints are sufficient.
